etymologies.text: 元(げん) (gen, “element”) + 素(そ) (so, “element”). Calque of Dutch hoofdstof.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Uncertain.
May be from written Chinese 冒頭 /冒头 (màotóu), analyzable as 冒 (“to emerge”) + 頭 (“the head; the top; the beginning”).
First attested in the 1880s in Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from verb 報(ほう)ずる (hōzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 天體 (MC then thejX). Analyzable as
天 (ten, “heaven”) + 体 (tai, “body”).

etymologies.text:
Originally a compound of 身(み) (mi, “body”) + 木(き) (ki, “tree”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 手法 (MC syuwX pjop). Compare modern Mandarin 手法 (shǒufǎ).

etymologies.heading: Etymology

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 棄 is a daiyōji replacing 毀.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. Appears in the earliest texts of the 700s CE, including the Nihon Shoki and the Man'yōshū. Ultimately from Proto-Japonic *muna.
Analyzable as むな (muna, “cavity, void, open space”, combining form, spelled variously as 空, 虚, 胸, 棟; cognate with standalone nouns 胸 (mune, “chest”), 棟 (mune, “roof ridge”)) + adjective-forming suffix しい (shii).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 素 (そ, so: “element”) + 材 (ざい, zai: “material”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 詫(わ)びる (wabiru, “to apologise”).

From Old Japanese, a compound of 宮(みや) (miya, “imperial palace”) + 処(こ) (ko, “place”).
